blocks.text: Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch of your Mac. In Safari, hold ⌥⌘, ask about the page, and Lazur answers out loud. It sees your screen only while you hold the keys. It does not click buttons for you. You stay in control of every click and keystroke.

Here is the short version of the rest of this page. Lazur explains what you see, points at controls, guides you through a task, and types or dictates text at the cursor. Each job starts with a different key or question. The sections below show a real example for each one, along with the mistakes people make.
What an AI assistant for Safari on Mac does in practice

Lazur has five jobs in Safari. It explains what is on screen. It points at things. It guides you one step at a time. It drafts text and types it where your cursor sits. It dictates when you hold fn. Each job starts with a different action on your part, so decide which one you need before you ask.

items: Explain: ask what a page, error, or setting means, and hear the answer out loud.
Point: ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it.
Guide: ask how to do a task, and Lazur gives one click at a time and waits for each click.
Draft and dictate: hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor, or ask Lazur to draft a reply.
Everyday tasks: timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music, opening links, and web search.

blocks.text: Research is the sixth job, and it runs differently. Longer research jobs run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. They come back with a summary and a report. They do not run inside your Safari window.
Ask what is on the page

The most common use is a question about the page you already have open. Say what you are looking at, then ask. Lazur answers from the screen at the moment you hold the keys. Ask in plain words. You do not need the technical name for the thing you see.

Here is a real case. Safari shows a message such as 'This site can't be reached' when you open a page you need. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask, 'Why won't this page load?' Lazur reads the message and explains the likely causes in plain words. Those causes can include a typo in the address, a site that is down, or a weak connection. You decide what to try next.

blocks.title: Bring the right tab forward
blocks.text: Lazur answers from what is on screen when you hold the keys. Bring the page you mean to the front first, then hold ⌥⌘. A question asked about the wrong tab gets a confident answer about the wrong page.
Point at a control you cannot find

Safari has many small controls. Some sit in menus that change between versions, so an old guide can mislead you. When you cannot find one, ask Lazur where it is. Lazur says where it is, out loud. It draws a circle and a label around the target on your screen. Then you click it yourself.

A useful example is Report a Website Issue. Apple's troubleshooting page says Safari 26 or later lets you send that report from the Page Menu. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask, 'Where is Report a Website Issue?' Lazur circles the Page Menu and labels it. Open the menu, then choose the item. Lazur does not open it for you.

Name the label, not the look. 'The Sign In button' gives Lazur a clear target. 'The blue button on the right' is harder to match. When a control has no text, describe what it does, such as 'the icon that opens settings for this page.'
Walk through a Safari fix one click at a time

Some tasks have a dozen small steps. Ask Lazur to guide you, and it gives one click at a time. It waits for each click before it gives the next step. That keeps you from skipping a step. You can stop halfway and ask again later.
Take a site that Safari blocks from opening a payment window. Ask, 'Walk me through letting this site open pop-up windows.' A guided run goes like this.

items: Click Safari in the menu bar, then choose Settings.
Click Websites at the top of the Settings window.
Choose Pop-up Windows in the left column.
Find this site in the list and set it to Allow.
Close Settings, return to the page, and try the payment again.

blocks.text: Each step is short on purpose. If a menu name differs on your Mac, say so. Lazur will point at the item that matches what you see on screen.

Allow pop-ups for one site, not every site. Turning off pop-up blocking everywhere lets unwanted windows open on every page you visit. A per-site setting keeps that protection on for the rest of the web.
Clear cookies or website data for one site

Apple lists sites that ask you to remove or reset cookies as a common Safari problem. Removing one site's data often fixes a stuck login or a page that loads wrong. Go to Safari > Settings > Privacy > Manage Website Data. Search for the site, select it, and remove its data.
Other sites keep their data. That is the reason to pick one site, not all of them. Clearing everything signs you out of most of the web at once, and getting back in takes time.

blocks.title: Save your work first
blocks.text: Removing a site's data signs you out there. If you have a half-written form or draft on that site, copy it first. Paste it into a note, then clear the data.
Where Safari problems start

Apple does not publish a ranking of its Safari help topics. No one outside Apple can say which problem is most common. The best guide is Apple's own troubleshooting page. It lists the problems people bring to support, and those problems show where Safari users get stuck.

items: Pages blank or not loading fully.
Sign-in failing even with the right credentials.
Sites asking you to remove or reset cookies.
Safari slowing, freezing, or quitting unexpectedly.
Unwanted pages reopening when Safari starts.

blocks.text: Each of those needs a different first move. A slow page and a sign-in failure are not fixed the same way. Start with the symptom in front of you, then use the matching section of this page.
The research behind this page found no public count of how often each problem is searched. Read the list as a set of likely problems, not a ranking.
Fix a page that will not load in Safari

Start with the simple moves. Reload the page with ⌘R. If it still fails, open a private window with ⇧⌘N and load the same address. A private window starts with no saved site data. If the page works there, the problem is probably stored data, not the site itself.

items: Press ⌘R to reload the page.
Press ⇧⌘N, paste the address, and load it in a private window.
If the private window works, clear website data for that one site.
If Safari freezes, press ⌥⌘Esc, choose Safari, and select Force Quit.
If the site still fails, open the Page Menu and choose Report a Website Issue.

blocks.text: Hold Shift while you open Safari if pages keep reopening on their own. Apple's steps use this trick to stop pages from loading at launch. Use it once, then open Safari normally.
Ask Lazur to walk you through the private window test one click at a time. That keeps you from skipping the step that tells you where the problem lives.
Sign-in fails even with the right password

Apple lists sign-in failing despite correct credentials as a common problem. Stored site data is a frequent cause. Test in a private window first. A private window does not carry your saved cookies, so you sign in again there from scratch.

If the sign-in works in private, clear that site's data in a normal window, then sign in again. If it still fails, ask Lazur to explain the error on the page. It reads the message out loud and suggests the next thing to check.
Lazur explains the message. It does not sign in for you, because it does not click or operate Safari.
Safari keyboard shortcuts to learn first

Shortcuts save time, and they often fix a problem faster than a menu. Apple's shortcut list covers the everyday ones. The table below lists the ones that matter most on this page, with a question you can ask Lazur when you forget one.

rows: How do I search this page?
How do I go back one page?
How do I close this tab?
How do I open a private window?
blocks.caption: Safari shortcuts from Apple's keyboard shortcut guide

blocks.title: Shortcuts vary by layout
blocks.text: Apple says shortcuts can vary by language and keyboard layout. If a shortcut does nothing, open the menu bar and look for the command there. Ask Lazur where it is.
Two more are worth a look. ⌃Tab moves to the next tab. ⌃⌘1 opens the Bookmarks sidebar. Apple lists both in its shortcut guide, next to the ones in the table.
Safari 27 and Mac compatibility

Safari 27 shipped on September 14, 2026, with macOS 27 Golden Gate. The current stable release is Safari 27.2, released October 26, 2026. Safari 27.3 is in beta. Apple's macOS 27 page lists Apple silicon Macs and MacBook Neo. It does not list Intel Macs.

Check your model before you upgrade. Lazur runs on Intel and Apple silicon Macs. Apple's macOS 27 list covers only Apple silicon, so an Intel Mac may not get macOS 27 at all. The steps in this guide assume Safari 27 menus. Older Safari menus can differ.

blocks.title: Match the guide to your version
blocks.text: Apple's Safari User Guide has a version selector. Pick your macOS version there to see the menu names that match your Mac.
Speed and battery: what the numbers mean

Apple says frequently visited sites load 35% faster in Safari than in Chrome. The test used 12 popular sites in a simulated network, on an M5 MacBook Air, against a prerelease Safari 27.0 build. It is Apple's own test. Treat it as a claim, not a measurement you can repeat at home.

StatCounter puts Safari at 7.83% of worldwide desktop browser use in October 2026. Chrome has 66.98%. That count covers all desktop browsers, not Macs only. It measures use, not how often people get stuck on a page.
Lazur sees your screen in any app, so it works with whichever browser you pick. Choose Safari for the speed and battery you want. Then use Lazur on top of it.
Dictate and draft text at the cursor in Safari

Hold fn to dictate. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text and types it at the cursor. That works in a Safari text box, a web mail reply, or a form. Dictation is unlimited on both Pro and Power plans, so use it freely.
Drafting works differently. Ask Lazur to draft a reply, and it writes the text and types it at the cursor. Read the words before you send. Lazur does not press Send. That step stays with you.

Lazur also keeps snippets, a personal dictionary, and clipboard slots. Use snippets for text you type often, such as a sign-off or an address. Add names and technical terms to the personal dictionary so dictation spells them right.
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant in Safari

items: Asking about a page that is behind another window. Bring the right tab forward first.
Expecting Lazur to press buttons. It points, and you click.
Clearing all website data when one site's data would fix the problem.
Pressing ⌘R again and again on a page that is still loading.
Trusting a number from the screen without checking it on the page.
Hunting for a shortcut in the wrong menu. Check the menu bar first.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes come from a wrong guess about what Lazur sees or does. Lazur sees the screen while you hold the keys, and it answers from that. It does not click, and it does not run Safari for you.
Privacy: what Lazur sees and sends

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. When you ask, audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to get an answer. Those providers do not store them. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, on your Mac.

blocks.title: Hold keys only when you need an answer
blocks.text: If a page shows private money or health details, close it or move it out of view before you hold ⌥⌘. Holding the keys is the only time Lazur looks.
Where to start with Lazur in Safari

Install Lazur from the [download page](/download), then open a page you already know in Safari. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask what it says. Next, ask where one button is. Then hold fn in a text box and dictate one sentence. Those three steps cover most first-day questions.

Lazur offers a free Pro trial with no credit card. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) before you decide. If you save a Google Sheet as PDF in Safari, the steps are in [how to export Google Sheets as PDF on Mac](/how-to/export-as-pdf-in-google-sheets).

faq.question: Is Lazur a Safari extension?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It is not a plugin, add-in, or extension for Safari or any other app. You hold ⌥⌘ in Safari, and Lazur answers out loud. It sees your screen only while you hold the keys.

faq.question: Can an AI assistant for Safari on Mac click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at a control and draws a circle and a label around it. For longer tasks, it guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. You do the clicking in every case.

faq.question: Which Macs can run Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Apple's macOS 27 page lists Apple silicon Macs and does not list Intel Macs, so check Apple's list before you upgrade.

faq.question: Which Safari version does this guide match?
faq.answer: This guide uses Safari 27, which shipped on September 14, 2026. Safari 27.2 is the current stable release, dated October 26, 2026. Menu names can change between versions, so check the menu bar if a step looks different.

faq.question: Does Lazur store what I say or the screenshot?
faq.answer: Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer your question. They are not stored there. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did on your Mac.

faq.question: Can I dictate into a Safari text box?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn and speak. Lazur dictates clean, formatted text at the cursor in Safari and other apps. Add names to the personal dictionary so the spelling comes out right.

faq.question: Is there a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur offers a free Pro trial with no credit card. Check the pricing page for current plans and limits before you decide.

faq.question: Why does Lazur sometimes answer about the wrong page?
faq.answer: Lazur answers from what is on screen when you hold the keys. Bring the page you mean to the front, then hold ⌥⌘ again. Asking at the right moment fixes most wrong answers.

faq.question: Does Lazur work in Chrome or Firefox too?
faq.answer: Lazur sees your screen in any app, so it can help with a page in any browser. Research jobs run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension.
